neighbours.label: the regime word in a limiting condition of physics or maths ('for small values', 'at low temperatures')
fire: The series converges quickly for small values of x.
Superconductivity only appears at low temperatures in these metals.
The formula is accurate for small angles but fails for large ones.
Helium remains liquid at low pressures even close to absolute zero.
This expansion is valid only for small perturbations of the orbit.
Classical mechanics breaks down at small distances inside the atom.
The binomial distribution approaches the Poisson for small probabilities.
Friction becomes negligible at low speeds in this model.
quiet: The series was named after the mathematician who studied it.
Superconductivity was discovered in mercury in 1911.
The formula was printed on the first page of the textbook.
Helium is the second lightest element in the universe.
This expansion was described in a paper published last year.
Classical mechanics was developed by Newton and his successors.
The binomial distribution counts successes in a fixed number of trials.
Friction is the force that resists motion between surfaces.
